title: A Different Pond
author: Bao Phi
hook: A father and son go fishing before dawn. The pond is in Minneapolis. The memory is in Vietnam.
themes: family-labor, father-son, fishing, food-sourcing, immigration, Vietnam

title: A House for Hermit Crab
author: Eric Carle
hook: Every month, Hermit Crab adds something new to his shell. By December, he has outgrown it entirely.
themes: calendar, change, growth, marine-biology, ocean, symbiosis

title: A Seed Grows
author: Antoinette Portis
hook: A single seed's complete journey from soil to sunflower to seed again — with a fold-out at the end that is the full-grown plant itself.

title: A-Ztec: A Bilingual Alphabet Book
author: Emmanuel Valtierra
hook: The alphabet told in Spanish, Nahuatl, Mayan, and other Mesoamerican languages — a reminder that American history goes 3,000 years deeper than the English alphabet.

title: Aggie and the Ghost
author: Matthew Forsythe
hook: Aggie's new house comes with a ghost — and they must negotiate house rules before they can coexist.

title: Alberto Salas Plays Paka Paka con la Papa
author: Sara Andrea Fajardo
hook: Alberto Salas hunts for wild potatoes in the Andes Mountains to preserve biodiversity before they go extinct — and potato conservation is more urgent than you think.

title: Alexander and the Terrible Horrible No Good Very Bad Day
author: Judith Viorst
hook: Alexander's day is a masterclass in catastrophizing — and the punchline is that some days are just bad, even in Australia.

title: Anything
author: Rebecca Stead
hook: How many anythings can you wish for? The spread that answers this question is one of the most visually abundant pages in recent children's books.

title: At the Window
author: Hope Lim
hook: Two neighbors connect through their apartment windows — and when one window goes dark, the child learns to open her own.
themes: community, friendship, loss, neighbors, observation, windows

title: Awe!
author: Jilanne Hoffman
hook: Awe is not just a feeling — it's a scientifically studied emotion that shrinks your sense of self, connects you to something larger, and makes you measurably kinder. This book opens that emotion for the youngest readers.

title: Bartleby
author: Matt Phelan
hook: Bartleby is a dapper polar bear who knows exactly who he is — and the book is a modern classic for children who feel the pressure to be someone different.

title: Beautiful Black Boy
author: Sophia Robinson
hook: A joyful, affirmational celebration of Black boyhood — every spread an explosion of color and pride, with words designed to live in a child's head.

title: Beautiful Oops
author: Barney Saltzberg
hook: Every rip, spill, and smudge becomes a new creation — the most joyful case for growth mindset ever bound between covers.

title: Before Colors
author: Javier Saez Castan
hook: Before there were colors, there was light — and this picture book is a physics lesson about perception disguised as a bedtime question.

title: Big
author: Vashti Harrison
hook: A baby girl grows up hearing the word 'big' used as a wound — and eventually turns it into a crown.

title: Blueberries for Sal
author: Robert McCloskey
hook: A little girl and a bear cub both follow the wrong mother in the blueberry patch — a perfect parallel story about summer food and staying close.

title: Brave Irene
author: William Steig
hook: Irene delivers a ballgown through a blizzard for her sick mother — and the snow is so real you feel it.

title: Caboose
author: Travis Jonker
hook: A hippo is always first in line — until the day she's banished to the back. What happens to a child who has always led?

title: Caps for Sale
author: Esphyr Slobodkina
hook: A peddler falls asleep under a tree with caps stacked on his head. Every monkey in the tree takes one.

title: Chicka Chicka Boom Boom
author: Bill Martin Jr.
hook: All 26 letters race up the coconut tree — a phonics party with a structural collapse and a rhythm that sticks for life.

title: Chooch Helped
author: Andrea L. Rogers
hook: Sissy's little brother Chooch helps with everything — whether anyone asked him to or not — and the frustration is exactly right.

title: Chrysanthemum
author: Kevin Henkes
hook: A girl named Chrysanthemum loves her name until school teaches her to be ashamed of it — and one teacher quietly gives it back.

title: Click Clack Moo: Cows That Type
author: Doreen Cronin
hook: The cows find a typewriter and write demands to the farmer — a barnyard negotiation that accidentally teaches labor history and the power of written language.

title: Clifford the Big Red Dog
author: Norman Bridwell
hook: Emily Elizabeth's love for her tiny puppy makes him the biggest dog in the world — and the town has to rearrange itself around Clifford.

title: Corduroy
author: Don Freeman
hook: A department store bear with a missing button waits for someone to love him — and a girl with not quite enough money proves that love doesn't need to be perfect.

title: Count on Me
author: Miguel Tanco
hook: A girl who sees math everywhere: in spider webs, in sliced oranges, in the way birds sit on a wire.
themes: beauty-in-math, daily-life, math, observation, parent-child, patterns

title: Cranky, Crabby Crow (Saves the World)
author: Corey R. Tabor
hook: Crow seems cranky and mean and scares everyone away — and he is actually on a top-secret mission that will stun his friends.

title: Creepy Carrots!
author: Aaron Reynolds
hook: Jasper Rabbit loves carrots. Then the carrots start following him. Or do they?
themes: carrots, fear, garden, humor, imagination, paranoia, problem-solving

title: Croco
author: Azul López
hook: Croco is stuck in a hole — and tries every solution imaginable before finding the one that actually works.

title: Dad
author: Christian Robinson
hook: Christian Robinson's love letter to his own father — depicting a dad who is vulnerable, imperfect, gentle, and deeply human.

title: Dad, I Miss You
author: Nadia Sammurtok
hook: An Inuit child misses their father — and the specific landscape of the Arctic holds both the missing and the love.

title: Dawn: Watch the World Awaken
author: Marc Martin
hook: Dawn breaks over a forest lake — and every creature's awakening is a precise observation of how nature opens each day.

title: Diary of a Spider
author: Doreen Cronin
hook: A spider's diary reveals the misunderstood life of arachnids — including web architecture, fly diplomacy, and the annual spider molt.

title: Diary of a Worm
author: Doreen Cronin
hook: A worm's diary reveals the underground world most children have never thought about — and makes soil ecology genuinely unforgettable.

title: Doctor De Soto
author: William Steig
hook: A mouse dentist treats a fox — and has to outwit the fox before the fox eats him at the end of the appointment.

title: Don't Eat the Birthday Boy!
author: Donna Barba Higuera
hook: A monster was assigned to scare a child — but the child is having a birthday party, and the monster has a problem.

title: Don't Let the Pigeon Drive the Bus
author: Mo Willems
hook: The bus driver asks you to keep the pigeon from driving — and the pigeon will try every rhetorical trick he knows.

title: Don't Trust Fish
author: Neil Sharpson
hook: Fish have been plotting against us the whole time — and this book is a warning delivered with the comedic timing of a master.

title: Dragons Love Tacos
author: Adam Rubin
hook: Dragons love tacos — but they have a fatal weakness for salsa that triggers the funniest consequence in picture book history.

title: Drawn Onward
author: Daniel Nayeri
hook: The text reads the same forward and backward — and so does grief, which takes you somewhere new while feeling like you're going in reverse.

title: Drum Dream Girl
author: Margarita Engle
hook: On an island where only boys played drums, one girl heard music anyway.
themes: barrier-breaking, Cuba, gender-roles, music, persistence, rhythm

title: Duck and Goose
author: Tad Hills
hook: Duck and Goose fight over a polka-dotted ball that turns out to be an egg — and figure out how to be friends despite the misunderstanding.

title: Enemy Pie
author: Derek Munson
hook: A boy spends a whole summer day with his enemy to make the pie work — and discovers his enemy isn't an enemy at all.

title: Every Monday Mabel
author: Jashar Awan
hook: Every Monday, Mabel drags her chair to the driveway to watch the garbage truck — and she doesn't care even slightly that her family thinks it's weird.

title: Everywhere, Wonder
author: Matthew Swanson
hook: A book that teaches your child to ask questions the way a scientist does: by looking harder at ordinary things.
themes: curiosity, natural-world, observation, scientific-inquiry, seasons, wonder

title: Extra Yarn
author: Mac Barnett
hook: Annabelle finds a box of yarn that never runs out — and knits color into a gray winter town until everyone has more than they need.

title: Fall Is for Beginnings
author: Rajani LaRocca
hook: The start of the school year is also the start of fall — and Ravi discovers that both arrivals bring more than he expected.

title: Fireworks
author: Matthew Burgess
hook: Two siblings count down a steamy July day to the fireworks — and the waiting is almost the whole point.
themes: anticipation, city, July-4th, light, siblings, summer

title: Fish and Wave
author: Sergio Ruzzier
hook: A fish and a wave are total opposites — and they become best friends anyway, which is the whole ocean in a sentence.

title: Fox Has a Problem
author: Corey R. Tabor
hook: Fox has a problem — and every animal friend he asks gives him a completely different solution, which makes the problem much, much bigger.

title: Fox Versus Fox
author: Corey R. Tabor
hook: Fox meets another Fox — and they are immediately competitive about everything, including who is more Fox-like.

title: Frederick
author: Leo Lionni
hook: While his mouse family stores food for winter, Frederick stores colors, words, and sunlight — and saves them all when the cold and dark close in.

title: Freight Train
author: Donald Crews
hook: A red caboose, an orange tank car, a yellow hopper car, and a black steam engine. Moving. Caldecott Honor.

title: Frog and Toad Are Friends
author: Arnold Lobel
hook: Five short stories about two very different friends — and the most loving argument for loyalty in early chapter book form.

title: From Seed to Plant
author: Gail Gibbons
hook: The complete plant life cycle from seed to flower to fruit to new seed — accurate, illustrated, and impossible to forget.

title: George and Martha
author: James Marshall
hook: Five short stories about two hippos who are best friends — and who test every assumption about what friendship requires.

title: Gigi and Ojiji
author: Melissa Iwai
hook: Gigi doesn't speak her grandfather's language — but they find a way to say everything that matters without words.

title: Good Golden Sun
author: Brendan Wenzel
hook: The sun's energy flows through an entire ecosystem in one day — from the top of the food chain to the bottom and back — in a book that is visually unlike anything else.

title: Goodnight Gorilla
author: Peggy Rathmann
hook: A gorilla steals the zookeeper's keys and sets every animal free for the night — told almost entirely in pictures.

title: Goodnight Moon
author: Margaret Wise Brown
hook: The most soothing two minutes in childhood — and a secret lesson in language pattern and the night sky.

title: Green Eggs and Ham
author: Dr. Seuss
hook: Sam-I-Am will not stop asking — and his relentless persuasion campaign is secretly a phonics lesson and an argument for open-mindedness.

title: Growing Vegetable Soup
author: Lois Ehlert
hook: A parent and child grow every vegetable in their soup from seed to pot — the farm-to-table story at its most elemental.

title: Grumpy Monkey
author: Suzanne Lang
hook: Jim Panzee does not want to be happy today — and no amount of cheerful advice will change that.

title: Hair Love
author: Matthew A. Cherry
hook: Daddy has never done Zuri's hair before. He watches tutorials, breaks a comb, and makes a mess. Then he gets it right.

title: Harold and the Purple Crayon
author: Crockett Johnson
hook: Harold draws his entire world into existence with one crayon — and when something goes wrong, he draws a solution.

title: Henry, Like Always
author: Jenn Bailey
hook: Henry's school day follows the exact same sequence every day — and the day it doesn't is the whole story.

title: Hot Dog
author: Doug Salati
hook: A city dog on the hottest day of summer finds his way to the shore — and the whole arc of relief is something any child who has ever been too warm will understand.
themes: dogs, heat, New-York-City, seasons, summer, urban-nature

title: How a House Is Built
author: Gail Gibbons
hook: Every step of building a house from blueprint to moving day — clear, accurate, and illustrated like a technical diagram a child can love.

title: How Dinosaurs Went Extinct: A Safety Guide
author: Ame Dyckman
hook: Dinosaurs went extinct because they didn't follow basic safety rules — and the evidence is presented with courtroom seriousness.

title: How Do Dinosaurs Say Goodnight
author: Jane Yolen
hook: Real dinosaur species have bedtime tantrums — and then, eventually, they go to sleep just like children.

title: How to Count to 1
author: Casper Salmon
hook: The instructions are simple: count to one. No higher. The math and the comedy are perfectly balanced.

title: How to Find a Fox
author: Nilah Magruder
hook: She goes into the woods to find a fox. She does not find one. She finds everything else.
themes: failure, foxes, observation, patience, tracking, woodland

title: How to Hatch: A Gosling's Guide to Breaking Free
author: Sara Holly Ackerman
hook: A gosling inside an egg narrates the exact scientific process of hatching — and the pep talk she gives herself along the way is both biologically accurate and genuinely encouraging.

title: I Did It!
author: Michael Emberley
hook: A little bear finally does something all by himself — and the brimming pride is completely out of proportion to the task, which is exactly right.

title: I Hear the Snow, I Smell the Sea
author: Janice Milusich
hook: A child experiences snow and sea through sound and smell rather than sight — and the world opens differently when you experience it through different senses.

title: I Like Myself!
author: Karen Beaumont
hook: A girl with wild curls declares everything she loves about herself and dares the world to disagree.

title: If You Give a Mouse a Cookie
author: Laura Numeroff
hook: One cookie triggers an unstoppable chain reaction — the funniest math lesson about cause and effect ever written.

title: If You Give a Pig a Pancake
author: Laura Numeroff
hook: A pig's pancake breakfast spirals into a day of cause-and-effect chaos — and along the way introduces maple syrup production and food science.

title: If You Plant a Seed
author: Kadir Nelson
hook: Plant a seed of selfishness and watch what grows. Plant a seed of kindness and watch what grows.

title: Iggy Peck, Architect
author: Andrea Beaty
hook: A boy who has been building things since he was two constructs a bridge out of shoes and string.

title: In a Small Small Pond
author: Denise Fleming
hook: A year at a small pond through the eyes of the creatures who live there — rhyme and pulp-paper art make ecology unforgettable.

title: In Every Life
author: Marla Frazee
hook: A wordless journey through a human life and an animal life running parallel — and the final pages will stop you completely.
themes: birth, community, death, family, life-cycle, seasons

title: Inch by Inch
author: Leo Lionni
hook: An inchworm survives by making himself useful — and every bird he measures is a real species with a real wingspan.

title: Invisible Things
author: Andy J. Pizza
hook: Everything important is invisible — and this book makes the invisible visible, one page at a time.

title: Is It Spring?
author: Kevin Henkes
hook: Spring announces itself haltingly — snow one day, buds the next — and the book captures the specific emotional experience of waiting for the season to finally arrive.

title: Ish
author: Peter Reynolds
hook: Ramon gives up drawing after his brother laughs — until his sister shows him a wall full of his ish drawings she has saved.

title: Jovita Wore Pants: The Story of a Mexican Freedom Fighter
author: Aida Salazar
hook: Jovita Idár disguised herself as a man to fight in the Mexican Revolution — and her journalism and medicine saved more lives than her rifle.

title: Jumanji
author: Chris Van Allsburg
hook: Two bored children start a board game and discover every move releases a real jungle animal into their house.

title: Knuffle Bunny
author: Mo Willems
hook: Trixie can't yet speak — but she knows the laundromat has her bunny, and getting the message across is the whole emergency.

title: Leo the Late Bloomer
author: Robert Kraus
hook: Leo can't read or draw or eat neatly — until one day he can, and the whole jungle breathes out.

title: Lilly's Purple Plastic Purse
author: Kevin Henkes
hook: Lilly adores her teacher until he takes her purse away — and then she writes him a note she immediately regrets.

title: Little Blue Truck
author: Alice Schertle
hook: Little Blue Truck greets every farm animal by name and gets stuck in the mud — and every friend he made rushes to push him free.

title: Lola
author: Karla Arenas Valenti
hook: Lola must make a choice between two spirits — one offering everything she wants, one asking for something she doesn't yet understand.

title: Loops
author: Jashar Awan
hook: A story told almost entirely through circles, loops, and spirals — each shape carrying the emotional weight of loneliness, frustration, and joy without a word needing to do the work.

title: Make Way for Ducklings
author: Robert McCloskey
hook: A mother duck navigates the city of Boston to find a safe home for her ducklings — and an entire city stops to help her do it.

title: Making Art
author: Diana Ejaita
hook: Making art is making meaning — and Ejaita's visual language draws from West African textile tradition to show a child why the process matters more than the product.

title: Mama Miti: Wangari Maathai and the Trees of Kenya
author: Donna Jo Napoli
hook: A Kenyan woman plants one tree, then convinces an entire country to plant thirty million more.

title: Maybe Something Beautiful
author: F. Isabel Campoy & Theresa Howell
hook: A gray neighborhood. A girl with paint. A muralist who says yes. The walls come alive.
themes: color, community-art, murals, neighborhood-transformation, San-Diego, urban-renewal

title: Menudo Sunday: A Spanglish Counting Book
author: María Dolores Águila
hook: Two abuelitos, three primos, four tías, and their dogs gather to make menudo on Sunday — and counting the family is as important as the recipe.

title: Mike Mulligan and His Steam Shovel
author: Virginia Lee Burton
hook: Mike and his steam shovel Mary Anne dig the town hall cellar in one day — and find that being useful takes many forms.

title: Miss Rumphius
author: Barbara Cooney
hook: Alice Rumphius travels the world and then scatters lupine seeds across the Maine coast — and makes the whole coast more beautiful.

title: Mistaco
author: Eliza Kinkz
hook: A girl can't roll a round tortilla to save her life — and her abuelo will eat every single misshapen one.

title: Mixed: A Colorful Story
author: Arree Chung
hook: Reds, Yellows, and Blues live together. Then they decide they are different. A mixed-color child changes everything.
themes: art, color-mixing, community, primary-colors, segregation, unity

title: My Daddy Is a Cowboy
author: Stephanie Seales
hook: A girl and her father take an early morning horseback ride through their city — six starred reviews for a book about just-us time that the Coretta Scott King committee found essential.

title: My Heart Fills with Happiness
author: Monique Gray Smith
hook: Bannock baking with a grandmother. Drumming and singing. These are the moments when a heart fills up.

title: Nell Plants a Tree
author: Anne Wynter
hook: Nell plants a tree — and the book follows that tree across 100 years of community life.

title: Night Walk
author: Jason Cockcroft
hook: A boy and his grandfather walk to Grandma's favorite place at night — and the walk is about loss and what the stars keep.

title: Nightsong
author: Sally Soweol Han
hook: A boy rides home on a bus and discovers the whole world is singing to him — the rain, the wind, the city — if he's still and listening.

title: Not a Box
author: Antoinette Portis
hook: It is not a box. It is a race car. It is not a box. It is a mountain. Except it is definitely a box.

title: Officer Buckle and Gloria
author: Peggy Rathmann
hook: Officer Buckle's safety speeches put everyone to sleep — until Gloria the police dog starts acting them out behind his back.

title: Once Upon a Book
author: Grace Lin
hook: A girl opens a book and falls directly into it — and the book inside the book is this one.

title: Our Lake
author: Angie Kang
hook: A community gathers around a lake through every season — and the lake holds them all.

title: Our Mothers' Names: Love in Many Languages
author: Uma Menon
hook: Children all over the world call their mothers something different — and the language they use holds the whole culture it comes from.

title: Over and Under the Pond
author: Kate Messner
hook: A mother and son paddle across a pond while an entire hidden world hunts and builds beneath their boat.

title: Over in the Meadow
author: John Langstaff
hook: A counting song about meadow animals and their young — ten mother-child pairs, ten different behaviors, one meadow ecosystem.

title: Owl and Penguin
author: Vikram Madan
hook: Owl loves night and Penguin loves day — and their schedule conflict is the funniest biology lesson in early reader history.

title: Owl at Home
author: Arnold Lobel
hook: Owl tries to befriend the moon, worries about bumps in the night, and makes tear-water tea — quiet, strange, and deeply comforting.

title: Owl Moon
author: Jane Yolen
hook: A child and her father hike into the snowy woods at night to find an owl — and the silence teaches more than any classroom could.

title: Papá's Magical Water-Jug Clock
author: Jesús Trejo
hook: A boy's father builds a clock out of water jugs — and the invention teaches both time measurement and the engineering of improvisation.

title: Pencil
author: Hye-Eun Kim
hook: A pencil and a child draw each other into being — and the concept of imagination as a creative loop opens the very nature of drawing.

title: Planting a Rainbow
author: Lois Ehlert
hook: A family plants bulbs in fall and watches every color of the rainbow bloom in spring — and every flower named is real.

title: Popo the Xolo
author: Paloma Angelina Lopez
hook: The xoloitzcuintli is the oldest dog breed in the Americas — and this is the story of one who has been a companion to people across 3,000 years of Mexican history.

title: Press Here
author: Herve Tullet
hook: Press the yellow dot. Turn the page. You did that. The first interactive book that uses no technology.

title: Rain!
author: Linda Ashman
hook: Same rain, two people, completely different days. The simplest lesson in perspective your child will ever get.
themes: empathy, mood, perspective, rain, urban-life, weather

title: Rosie Revere, Engineer
author: Andrea Beaty
hook: A quiet girl who builds inventions in secret learns from her great-great-aunt that the only real failure is quitting.

title: Roxaboxen
author: Alice McLerran
hook: Children in an Arizona town build a city from stones and bottles in the desert — and it becomes more real than the real town.

title: Runaway Bunny
author: Margaret Wise Brown
hook: A little bunny runs away in every possible form — and his mother follows through mountains and rivers and air until he gives up and stays.

title: Sam and Dave Dig a Hole
author: Mac Barnett
hook: Sam and Dave dig straight down looking for something spectacular — and pass right by diamonds without knowing it.

title: Stellaluna
author: Janell Cannon
hook: A young bat falls from her mother's arms and must live as a bird — until she discovers that being herself is better than fitting in.

title: Stop That Mop!
author: Jonathan Fenske
hook: The mop is out of control, and nobody told it the rules — comedy and cause-and-effect logic for beginning readers.

title: Sulwe
author: Lupita Nyong'o
hook: A girl whose skin is the color of midnight learns that the night sky is where stars live.
themes: beauty-standards, colorism, Kenyan-culture, night-sky, self-acceptance, skin-color, stars

title: Sunday
author: Marcelo Tolentino
hook: Sunday is the slow day — the day that belongs to the whole family — and this book makes you feel what that rest actually means.

title: Swimmy
author: Leo Lionni
hook: A small black fish leads his red school to swim together in the shape of a giant fish — and teaches camouflage and cooperation in one image.

title: Sylvester and the Magic Pebble
author: William Steig
hook: Sylvester finds a magic pebble and turns himself into a rock — and has to wait through every season until his family's grief accidentally saves him.

title: Teaching for Change: How Septima Clark Led the Civil Rights Movement to Voting Justice
author: Yvonne Clark-Rhines and Monica Clark-Robinson
hook: Septima Clark taught thousands of Black Southerners to read and write — because in 1960s America, you couldn't register to vote if you couldn't pass a literacy test.

title: The Arguers
author: Corinna Luyken
hook: A new fairy tale that feels as old as time — about two characters who are relentlessly, hilariously, unstoppably arguing — from one of the most visually distinctive voices in children's books.

title: The Bear Out There
author: Jess Hannigan
hook: A know-it-all girl explains everything about the bear outside — and the reader can see from the very first page that she's completely wrong.

title: The Big Red Barn
author: Margaret Wise Brown
hook: A farm day from morning to night — every animal named, every sound captured, the whole cycle complete.

title: The Biggest Bear
author: Lynd Ward
hook: Johnny brings home a bear cub — and learns the hard way that wild animals and farms don't mix for long.

title: The Book With No Pictures
author: B.J. Novak
hook: A book that forces adults to say increasingly ridiculous things out loud — and proves that words alone are entertainment.

title: The Carrot Seed
author: Ruth Krauss
hook: A boy plants a carrot seed while everyone tells him it won't grow — and it grows.

title: The Day the Crayons Quit
author: Drew Daywalt
hook: Duncan's crayons each have a grievance — and their letters reveal color theory, fair use, and the full spectrum of artistic frustration.

title: The Dot
author: Peter H. Reynolds
hook: A girl who says she cannot draw makes a single dot. Then everything changes.
themes: art, creativity, growth, mentorship, self-doubt, self-expression

title: The Garden of Abdul Gasazi
author: Chris Van Allsburg
hook: A boy chases a dog into a forbidden garden — and comes out unsure of what is real.

title: The Giving Tree
author: Shel Silverstein
hook: A tree gives everything she has to a boy she loves across a lifetime — and the book refuses to tell you how to feel about it.

title: The Hair Book
author: Andrea J. Brown-Wood
hook: A celebration of Black hair through generations — the verse goes straight to the heart and the art is a loving archive of Black beauty across time.

title: The Hello Goodbye Window
author: Norton Juster
hook: The kitchen window at Nanna and Poppy's house is where everything happens — hello, goodbye, and all the in-between.

title: The Honey Bee
author: Kirsten Hall
hook: A poem that hums. Your child will never look at a flower the same way after this one.
themes: bees, community-labor, food-systems, interdependence, pollination, seasons

title: The Keeping Quilt
author: Patricia Polacco
hook: A quilt made from immigrant clothing travels through four generations — a family history you can touch.

title: The Lighthouse Keeper
author: Eugenio Fernández Vázquez
hook: A lighthouse keeper and the sailors his light guides — a meditation on purpose and solitude that has astonishing visual depth.

title: The Listening Walk
author: Paul Showers
hook: A girl and her father walk through the neighborhood without talking, and the world gets incredibly loud.

title: The Little House
author: Virginia Lee Burton
hook: A little house watches the city grow up around her across a century — and finally finds her way back to the countryside.

title: The Lorax
author: Dr. Seuss
hook: The Once-ler builds an industry that destroys an ecosystem — and a small orange creature tries to stop him one tree at a time.

title: The Napping House
author: Audrey Wood
hook: Everyone in the napping house piles on top of everyone else — until a tiny flea wakes the whole stack.

title: The Pout-Pout Fish
author: Deborah Diesen
hook: A glum fish believes he was born to spread dreary wearies — until a stranger's kiss changes his whole understanding of himself.

title: The Recess Queen
author: Alexis O'Neill
hook: Mean Jean rules recess — until a new girl asks her to jump rope, and genuine friendliness resets the whole playground.

title: The Relatives Came
author: Cynthia Rylant
hook: The relatives drive up from Virginia for the summer and fill every corner of the house — and the reunion is so warm it practically radiates off the page.

title: The Snail and the Whale
author: Julia Donaldson
hook: A tiny snail hitches a ride on a whale's tail and sees the whole world, until the whale needs the snail to save her.

title: The Truth about Dragons
author: Julie Leung
hook: Western dragons hoard gold and breathe fire; Eastern dragons bring rain and good fortune — and both are true.

title: The Ugly Five
author: Julia Donaldson
hook: The wildebeest, hyena, vulture, warthog, and marabou stork are the ugliest animals on the savanna, and their babies think they are beautiful.

title: The Very Hungry Caterpillar
author: Eric Carle
hook: One tiny egg becomes a butterfly — and along the way teaches counting and one of biology's most astonishing transformations.

title: The Very Quiet Cricket
author: Eric Carle
hook: A cricket who can't yet chirp meets creature after creature — and the wait for his first sound teaches patience, communication, and insect biology.

title: The Water Princess
author: Susan Verde
hook: Based on Georgie Badiel's childhood in Burkina Faso, a girl walks miles for water.

title: The Way I Feel
author: Janan Cain
hook: One emotion per page, fully inhabited — the most precise emotional vocabulary primer for young children.

title: The Yellow Bus
author: Loren Long
hook: A school bus ages out of her route and finds unexpected new purpose — as shelter for the unhoused, home for goats, reef for fish.
themes: aging, change, community, environment, purpose, time

title: There Was a Party for Langston
author: Jason Reynolds

themes: Black-girlhood, civil-rights-era, family, identity, memoir, New-York, South-Carolina, writing

title: Brown Girl Dreaming
author: Jacqueline Woodson
hook: Jacqueline Woodson grew up between Ohio and South Carolina with the Civil Rights Movement happening outside her window.
themes: civil-rights, family, identity, Jim-Crow, memoir, poetry

title: Chasing Lincoln's Killer
author: James L. Swanson
hook: John Wilkes Booth shot Abraham Lincoln at 10:15 PM on April 14, 1865 — and for 12 days evaded the largest manhunt in American history, with a broken leg.

title: Chasing Space: An Astronaut's Story of Grit, Grace, and Second Chances
author: Leland Melvin
hook: Leland Melvin was drafted by the NFL and went deaf in NASA training — and still made it to the International Space Station twice.

title: City Spies
author: James Ponti
hook: Five kids from five different countries, each with a skill set no adult spy could fake — and MI6 recruits them to go where trained agents cannot.

title: Code Girls: The Untold Story of the American Women Codebreakers of World War II (Young Readers Edition)
author: Liza Mundy
hook: Thousands of American women were secretly recruited to crack enemy codes in WWII — doing mathematics that shortened the war — and the government kept it classified for decades.

title: Discovering Life's Story: The Birth of Genetics
author: Joy Hakim
hook: The story of how humans figured out that traits are inherited, from Gregor Mendel's peas to the discovery of DNA — and how long it took, and how many people were wrong first.

title: Drowned City: Hurricane Katrina and New Orleans
author: Don Brown
hook: Hurricane Katrina hit New Orleans on August 29, 2005 — and the real disaster was not the storm, but the levees that were supposed to protect the city.

title: El Deafo
author: Cece Bell
hook: Cece Bell lost her hearing at 4 from meningitis — and got the biggest hearing aid any child had ever worn, which she eventually realized gave her a superpower.

title: Escape from Mr. Lemoncello's Library
author: Chris Grabenstein
hook: A famous game designer built the most extraordinary library ever — and 12 kids are locked inside for the night to solve puzzles using only the books on the shelves.

title: Fallout: Spies, Superbombs, and the Ultimate Cold War Showdown
author: Steve Sheinkin
hook: The hydrogen bomb was 1,000 times more powerful than the atom bomb — and as America built it, Soviet spies stole the secrets, and the world reached the edge of annihilation.

title: Footeprint: Eunice Newton Foote at the Dawn of Climate Science and Women's Rights
author: Lindsay H. Metcalf
hook: Eunice Newton Foote discovered the greenhouse effect in 1856 and was erased from history so completely that it took 150 years for anyone to notice — this is the novel that refuses to let that stand.

title: From the Mixed-Up Files of Mrs. Basil E. Frankweiler
author: E.L. Konigsburg
hook: Two siblings secretly live inside the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York City — and stumble onto a mystery about a statue that may be by Michelangelo.

title: Greenglass House
author: Kate Milford
hook: A smugglers' inn on a cliff above a frozen river fills with mysterious guests during Christmas break.

title: Guts
author: Raina Telgemeier
hook: Raina woke up one morning with a terrible stomach ache — and the stomach ache never really went away. This is the graphic memoir of what anxiety feels like from the inside.

title: Hidden Figures Young Readers' Edition
author: Margot Lee Shetterly
hook: Before NASA had computers, it had human computers — women who did the math by hand. The ones nobody wrote about were Black, and they were brilliant.

title: Hilo: The Boy Who Crashed to Earth
author: Judd Winick
hook: A boy from another planet crash-lands on Earth with no idea where he came from — and his new best friend has to help him figure out what he is before the things chasing him arrive.

title: How to Be a Good Creature: A Memoir in Thirteen Animals
author: Sy Montgomery
hook: Thirteen animals — pigs, octopuses, emus, tarantulas — each one teaching Sy Montgomery something essential about being alive that she could not have learned from a human.

title: Howl's Moving Castle
author: Diana Wynne Jones
hook: Sophie is cursed to be an old woman and walks into the moving castle of the most dreadful wizard in the land — who turns out to be very different from what everyone says.

title: I Will Always Write Back: How One Letter Changed Two Lives
author: Caitlin Alifirenka and Martin Ganda with Liz Welch
hook: A girl from Pennsylvania and a boy from Zimbabwe started writing to each other as a sixth-grade assignment — and the exchange revealed two completely different worlds.

title: Impossible Escape: A True Story of Survival and Heroism in Nazi Europe
author: Steve Sheinkin
hook: Rudolf Vrba escaped from Auschwitz — one of fewer than 700 people who ever did — and raced to get the truth to the world before Hungary's 750,000 Jews were deported there to die.

title: Inkheart
author: Cornelia Funke
hook: A man who can read characters out of books accidentally read a villain out of a novel 12 years ago — and now his daughter Meggie discovers she has the same power.

title: Island of the Blue Dolphins
author: Scott O'Dell
hook: Karana is left behind when her people evacuate from a remote Pacific island — and survives alone for 18 years, becoming one of the most extraordinary figures in California history.

title: Legendary Frybread Drive-In: Intertribal Stories
author: edited by Cynthia Leitich Smith
hook: Indigenous authors from across more than a dozen nations tell the stories of Native American teenagers — and the anthology's title alone teaches that Native American culture is not one thing, it is hundreds.

title: Lincoln's Grave Robbers
author: Steve Sheinkin
hook: A gang of counterfeiters plots to steal Abraham Lincoln's body from his Springfield tomb in 1876 — and the Secret Service has to stop them without Lincoln's family finding out.

title: Maniac Magee
author: Jerry Spinelli
hook: Jeffrey Magee runs so fast he becomes a legend — and runs across the invisible line dividing his Pennsylvania town into two worlds that have forgotten they were once one.

title: Messy Roots
author: Laura Gao
hook: Laura Gao grew up caught between Wuhan and Texas, and then her hometown became the most hated word in America.

title: Most Dangerous: Daniel Ellsberg and the Secret History of the Vietnam War
author: Steve Sheinkin
hook: Daniel Ellsberg had access to the most classified document in America — 7,000 pages of evidence that the government had been lying about Vietnam for 20 years — and had to decide what to do with it.

title: Mrs. Frisby and the Rats of NIMH
author: Robert C. O'Brien
hook: A widowed mouse needs to save her sick son — and the only ones who can help are a colony of superintelligent rats who escaped from a government laboratory.

title: Never Caught, the Story of Ona Judge
author: Erica Armstrong Dunbar and Kathleen Van Cleve
hook: Ona Judge was enslaved in George Washington's household — and on a May evening in 1796, she walked out the front door and never came back. Washington spent years trying to recapture her.

title: Omnivore's Dilemma: Young Readers Edition
author: Michael Pollan
hook: Where does your food actually come from — and what does the answer reveal about modern agriculture, ecology, and what it means to eat?

title: Port Chicago 50: Disaster, Mutiny, and the Fight for Civil Rights
author: Steve Sheinkin
hook: 50 Black Navy sailors refused dangerous orders after an explosion killed 320 of their servicemen — and were charged with mutiny, launching one of the most important civil rights cases of WWII.

title: Radium Girls (Young Readers Edition)
author: Kate Moore
hook: Young women who painted watch dials with radium paint in the 1920s were told to lick their brushes — and the science of what happened next changed labor law in America forever.

title: Ranger's Apprentice: The Ruins of Gorlan
author: John Flanagan
hook: Will is chosen as apprentice to a Ranger — the king's secret corps of trackers and archers — and discovers that being small and overlooked is the greatest advantage a spy can have.

title: Reaching for the Moon: The Autobiography of NASA Mathematician Katherine Johnson
author: Katherine Johnson
hook: Katherine Johnson's own account — in her own words — of growing up in segregated West Virginia, falling in love with math, and calculating the trajectory that sent humans to the moon.

title: Redwall
author: Brian Jacques
hook: A young mouse must find the legendary sword of the great Martin the Warrior to defend Redwall Abbey from a rat warlord — and he is nobody's idea of a hero.

title: Rising Water: The Story of the Thai Cave Rescue
author: Marc Aronson
hook: 12 boys and their soccer coach trapped in a flooding cave in Thailand in 2018 — and the international rescue operation that required inventing a solution that had never been attempted.

title: Shipwreck at the Bottom of the World
author: Jennifer Armstrong
hook: Shackleton's ship was crushed by Antarctic ice. He kept 27 men alive for two years on floating ice.

title: Spy School
author: Stuart Gibbs
hook: Ben Ripley is recruited to a secret CIA academy as bait to catch a dangerous enemy agent — and he has absolutely no idea what he's doing, which turns out to be his greatest asset.

title: Steve Jobs: The Man Who Thought Different
author: Karen Blumenthal
hook: Steve Jobs changed what a computer looks like and what it feels like to use one — and the biography is honest about what that cost him and the people around him.

title: Temple Grandin
author: Sy Montgomery
hook: Temple Grandin thinks in pictures, not words. That is why she understands cows better than any human alive.

title: The Boys Who Challenged Hitler: Knud Pedersen and the Churchill Club
author: Phillip Hoose
hook: In 1941, Danish teenagers formed the Churchill Club, sabotaged German vehicles and supply depots, got arrested, and kept resisting from prison.

title: The Brilliant Deep: Rebuilding the World's Coral Reefs
author: Kate Messner
hook: Ken Nedimyer decided to regrow the coral reef off the Florida Keys by hand, one fragment at a time — and the science of rebuilding a living ecosystem from scratch is extraordinary.

title: The City of Ember
author: Jeanne DuPrau
hook: Ember is the only city in the world — it has always been the only city — and its lights are failing. Two teenagers figure out why and what lies beyond the darkness.

title: The Dark Lord of Derkholm
author: Diana Wynne Jones
hook: A demon tourist company brings busloads of tourists from another world to see a real Dark Lord and a quest — and it is absolutely destroying the place.

title: The Evolution of Calpurnia Tate
author: Jacqueline Kelly
hook: In 1899 Texas, a girl discovers Darwin's Origin of Species and realizes the world she is being prepared for and the world she lives in are two different species.

title: The Fourteenth Goldfish
author: Jennifer L. Holm
hook: Ellie's grandfather discovers the secret to reversing aging and turns himself into a teenager.

title: The Great Fire
author: Jim Murphy
hook: The Great Chicago Fire of 1871 burned for two days, destroyed 17,000 buildings, and killed 300 people — and how it started is only the beginning of what the fire reveals.

title: The Hive Detectives: Chronicle of a Honey Bee Catastrophe
author: Loree Griffin Burns
hook: In 2006, beekeepers started finding their hives empty — millions of bees vanishing overnight — and scientists had no idea why.

title: The Last Kids on Earth
author: Max Brallier
hook: Jack Sullivan lives alone in his tree house after the zombie apocalypse with a monster pet and a baseball bat — and this is the greatest time of his life.

title: The Longitude Prize
author: Joan Dash
hook: For centuries, sailors could not determine their longitude at sea — and ships wrecked by the thousands. A clockmaker named John Harrison built the solution, and the scientific establishment spent decades refusing to accept it.

title: The Mysterious Benedict Society
author: Trenton Lee Stewart
hook: Four extraordinary children pass impossible tests to form a secret society — and their mission is to infiltrate an institute that may be brainwashing the world.

title: The Parker Inheritance
author: Varian Johnson
hook: A girl finds a 50-year-old letter hidden in her grandmother's house — and following its clues opens a buried civil rights injustice in their South Carolina town.

title: The Sign of the Beaver
author: Elizabeth George Speare
hook: Matt is left alone in colonial Maine while his father gets the rest of the family — and his survival depends on what a Penobscot boy named Attean is willing to teach him.

title: The Storm Runner
author: Jennifer Cervantes
hook: Zane lives in New Mexico near a dormant volcano — and a strange dog leads him into the Maya underworld, where he discovers his father is a god.

title: The Westing Game
author: Ellen Raskin
hook: Sam Westing is dead and has left 16 very different heirs — each holding one clue — to solve the puzzle of who killed him and claim $200 million.

title: The Witch of Blackbird Pond
author: Elizabeth George Speare
hook: Kit Tyler arrives in colonial Connecticut from Barbados and immediately breaks every rule of Puritan society — and when a friend is accused of witchcraft, it becomes her trial too.

title: They Called Us Enemy
author: George Takei
hook: George Takei was four years old when the US government sent his family to internment camps because they were Japanese American — and he draws exactly what he remembers.

title: Tracking Trash: Flotsam, Jetsam, and the Science of Ocean Motion
author: Loree Griffin Burns
hook: In 1990, a container ship spilled 80,000 Nike sneakers into the Pacific — and an oceanographer realized the shoes could tell him exactly how ocean currents work.

title: Tristan Strong Punches a Hole in the Sky
author: Kwame Mbalia
hook: Tristan accidentally tears a hole between the real world and Alke — a land made of American folk heroes and African gods — and must fight to repair it with Anansi as his reluctant guide.

title: Undefeated: Jim Thorpe and the Carlisle Indian School Football Team
author: Steve Sheinkin
hook: Jim Thorpe and the Carlisle Indian School took on the most powerful football programs in America in 1912 — and beat them all while also fighting a century of forced assimilation policy.

title: Watership Down
author: Richard Adams
hook: A colony of rabbits is warned of a coming disaster and sets out across the English countryside to find a new home — and builds a civilization along the way.

title: We Are Not Free
author: Traci Chee (editor)
hook: 14 authors, 14 Japanese American teenagers, all facing the same thing: forced removal into internment camps in WWII — each told in a completely different voice.

title: When You Reach Me
author: Rebecca Stead
hook: A girl in 1970s New York City starts receiving notes from someone who knows things about the future — and the mystery is quietly about time itself.

title: Women in Science: 50 Fearless Pioneers Who Changed the World
author: Rachel Ignotofsky
hook: 50 women who changed science across every field — from ancient astronomy to modern genetics — in illustrated profiles that make each one feel like someone you want to know.
